title: The Chain: Install → Discovery → Model → Entitlement → Result

narrations.text: The SAM Chain. Install → Discovery Model → Software Model → Entitlement → Reconciliation → Compliance
If you confuse these six record types, your compliance reports are fiction. Memorize the chain: I-D-S-E-R.

The Complete Chain (Memorize This Order). CI (CMDB/IRE) └─ cmdbsamswinstall Install └─ cmdbsamswdiscoverymodel Discovery Model └─ cmdbsoftwareproductmodel Software Model └─ almlicense Entitlement └─ reconciliation Result Mnemonic: I-D-S-E-R = Install → Discovery → Software Model → Entitlement → Reconciliation

Six Record Types — Never Confuse These. Software Model cmdbsoftwareproductmodel Canonical product definition Content Library / Admin Discovery Model cmdbsamswdiscoverymodel Raw fingerprint from field Discovery / SCCM / Intune Installation cmdbsamswinstall One install on one device Discovery import Usage sampswusage Evidence it was actually run Usage connectors Entitlement almlicense Right to use N units (metric) SAM Admin Reconciliation Result sampresult Computed compliance verdict Reconciliation job

The Three Most Confused Records. Software Model = Normalized, canonical definition (e.g., 'Microsoft Office Professional Plus 2019') Discovery Model = Raw observed string (e.g., 'Office16 ProPlus', 'O365ProPlus', 'MSOffice2019') Installation = Concrete instance on a specific CI (device), links to both above Without normalization: 40 Office variants → reconciliation chaos. Normalization converts Discovery Models → Software Models. Then Installs link to Software Models.
Critical: sampswusage is PRODUCT-LEVEL (publisher + product + CI + user) It does NOT reference the install row directly. It feeds reconciliation for reclamation decisions.

Three Reconciliation Tiers. Product sampproductresult Is the product compliant? Cost/savings? Software Model Software Model Results Which model is the problem? License Metric samplicensemetricresult Rights owned vs used vs available
